locator.section: 4.9 Radical site rearrangements (gamma-H rearrangement to an unsaturated group with beta-cleavage)

evidence.curator_note: Book draws 3 arc(s) for a full gamma-H ATOM transfer through the six-membered ring: (a) a fishhook from the odd electron on the n-ionized carbonyl oxygen (printed '+.' on O, C=O drawn intact) reaching to the gamma-hydrogen, (b) a long fishhook from the gamma C-H bond into the forming O-H bond, and (c) a fishhook from that same C-H bond back onto the gamma-carbon C(6). ENCODING NOTE (honest divergence from the drawing): the migrating hydrogen cannot be atom-mapped -- RDKit's SMILES parser folds any mapped explicit H into implicit valence -- so the C-H and O-H bonds are invisible to the bond-order bookkeeping. The electron_moves therefore encode the single change that survives at the heavy-atom level, namely the odd electron relocating from O(2) to the gamma-carbon C(6), which is exactly the net spin change the three drawn arcs accomplish (the page calls the product a 'distonic radical ion', i.e. the radical site has moved from O to the gamma-carbon while the H moved the other way). The transferred H is recorded by hydrogen_shift on the detected peak. C=O and the +charge on oxygen are retained (oxocarbenium =O+(H)). Instantiated with R = CH3 (parent = hexan-2-one).

Book draws 2 arc(s); moves <1,2> are drawn, move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). Drawn: (1) a fishhook from the radical on the gamma-carbon C(6) into the forming C(5)=C(6) pi bond, and (2) a fishhook from the C(4)-C(5) sigma bond (the beta C-C bond; the arrow itself is labelled 'alpha' on the page) into that same C(5)=C(6) pi bond. Implicit: (3) the second electron of the C(4)-C(5) bond returning to the alpha-carbon C(4), leaving the radical there -- the enol radical cation is simply drawn with its dot already on C(4). Products: the acetone enol radical cation (charge retained, m/z 58) plus neutral propene (R = CH3). The page draws the m/z 58 ion in its two resonance forms joined by a double-headed arrow -- the distonic form .CH2-C(=O+H)-CH3 (charge on O, radical on C4, encoded here) and the conventional form CH2=C(O+.H)-CH3 (radical+charge on O, C=C toward the carbonyl carbon); the encoded arrows produce exactly the distonic form.

Cross-linked MOD rule variables, verified against this scheme rather than asserted. IMS_4_33_rH DFS '[C]1[C]2([H]3)[C]4[C]5[C]6([C]7){=}[O+.]8>>[C]1[C.]2[C]4[C]5[C]6([C]7){=}[O+]8[H]3' maps exactly onto the rH step: it moves H(3) from the gamma-carbon C(2) to the oxygen O(8), keeps the C(6)=O(8) double bond, and leaves the charge on O with the odd electron now on the gamma-carbon C(2) -- the same net change encoded here (their C2/C6/O8/H3 = my C6/C1/O2/migrating-H). Note the MOD rule DOES atom-map the migrating H (index 3) because MOD's term graphs are not subject to RDKit H-folding; the JSON record cannot, hence the single net arrow above. IMS_4_33_alpha_1 DFS '[C]1[C.]2[C]3[C]4[C]5([C]6){=}[O+]7[H]8>>[C]1[C]2{=}[C]3.[C.]4[C]5([C]6){=}[O+]7[H]8' matches the alpha step: the gamma-radical C(2) forms the C(2)=C(3) pi bond, the beta C(3)-C(4) sigma bond cleaves, the alpha-carbon C(4) keeps the radical and the charge stays on O -- i.e. the cleaved bond IS incident to the pi-forming atom, giving the distonic enol radical cation exactly as drawn. RULE MISMATCH: IMS_4_33_alpha_2 DFS '...>>[C]1[C]2{=}[C]3.[C.]4{=}[C]5([C]6)[O+.]7[H]8' is intended as the resonance-partner encoding (C=C toward the carbonyl carbon, radical+charge on O) but is mis-encoded -- it writes BOTH a radical on the alpha-carbon C(4) AND the C(4)=C(5) double bond, so its product is a C3H5O diradical cation (m/z 57), not the m/z 58 enol radical cation, and it raises the unpaired-electron count from 1 (LHS) to 2 (RHS); it should be dropped by the L->R conservation guardrail. Only IMS_4_33_alpha_1 faithfully reproduces the drawn charge-retention product.
